other_us_indications: active psoriatic arthritis (adults) 2017-12-01; ankylosing spondylitis (adults) 2019-08-23; pediatric plaque psoriasis (6 to <18 years) 2020-03-26; non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (adults) 2020-05-29

company_at_launch: Eli Lilly and Company (U.S. and rest of world excluding Europe); Almirall in Europe
mechanism: IgG4 monoclonal antibody that binds IL-13 and inhibits signalling through the IL-4Ra/IL-13Ra1 complex (interleukin-13 antagonist)
dosing: 500 mg at weeks 0 and 2, 250 mg every 2 weeks until week 16 or later, then 250 mg every 4 weeks (250 mg every 8 weeks also approved 2026-06-09)
first_us_indication: Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older weighing at least 40 kg not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies
other_us_indications: none as of 2026-11-19 (S-006 2026-06-09 added a 250 mg every-8-weeks maintenance option, not a new indication)
notes: Lebrikizumab was licensed by Roche/Genentech (worldwide rights; Roche receives royalties) and came to Lilly with the Dermira acquisition (February 2020). Almirall holds the licence for Europe (EU approval Q4 2023) and sells it there; Lilly books royalties and milestones from Almirall as collaboration and other revenue inside its Ebglyss line (e.g. $65 million EU approval/launch milestones in Q4 2023). Japan approval reported in Lilly's Q4 2023 release (February 2024); Lilly's 2023 10-K lists Ebglyss for atopic dermatitis 'in Japan and, in collaboration with Almirall S.A., in Europe'. Lilly's printed Ebglyss revenue therefore is not product sales alone, especially before 2025. Window = 2023Q3 (first Lilly-printed Ebglyss revenue) to 2026Q3 (latest reported; 9th U.S. quarter).
